title: Coding finite sequences: pairing and bounded decoding

based_on.title: Computability and Incompleteness
based_on.pages: 28–30 (§2.4, finite sequences, bounds, and simultaneous/history recursion; version 2007-01-09)

based_on.title: Formalizing Computability Theory via Partial Recursive Functions
based_on.venue: 10th International Conference on Interactive Theorem Proving (ITP 2019)
based_on.pages: 12:2–12:7 (§§2–3.1, square pairing and primitive-recursive data operations)

summary: Encode finite lists as natural numbers, prove explicit decoding bounds, and derive primitive-recursive list operations and recursion on finite histories.
abstract: An algorithm working with a list must be able to read its entries, find its length and join it to another list. All these tasks can be performed on natural numbers once finite lists have numerical codes. We construct a coding in which every number represents exactly one list, and decoding each successive entry decreases the remaining code. This gives explicit bounds for the loops that compute length, indexed access, reversal and concatenation, proving that these operations are primitive recursive. Keeping several values or a whole finite history in one code then lets ordinary primitive recursion update them together or consult earlier results.
